# Top AI CEOs, experts raise 'risk of extinction' from AI

By [Supantha Mukherjee](https://www.reuters.com/authors/supantha-mukherjee/)

May 30, 2023 2:34 PM UTC Updated May 30, 2023

*

REUTERS/Florence Lo/Illustration/File Photo [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/illustration-picture-of-chatgpt/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjM6bmV3c21sX1JDMjQ2MUE3RTUzVw%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

STOCKHOLM, May 30 (Reuters) - Top artificial intelligence executives including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Tuesday joined experts and professors in raising the "risk of extinction from AI", which they urged policymakers to equate at par with risks posed by pandemics and nuclear war.

"Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war," more than 350 signatories wrote in a letter [published, opens new tab](https://www.safe.ai/statement-on-ai-risk) by the nonprofit Center for AI Safety (CAIS).

As well as Altman, they included the CEOs of AI firms DeepMind and Anthropic, and executives from Microsoft [(MSFT.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/companies/MSFT.O/) and Google [(GOOGL.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/companies/GOOGL.O/).

Also among them were Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio - two of the three so-called "godfathers of AI" who received the 2018 Turing Award for their work on deep learning - and professors from institutions ranging from Harvard to China's Tsinghua University.

A [statement, opens new tab](https://www.safe.ai/press-release) from CAIS singled out Meta [(META.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/companies/META.O/), where the third godfather of AI, Yann LeCun, works, for not signing the letter.

The letter coincided with the U.S.-EU Trade and Technology Council meeting in Sweden where politicians are expected to talk about [regulating AI](https://www.reuters.com/technology/eu-us-weigh-china-ai-trade-strains-high-level-sweden-talks-2023-05-30/).

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Elon Musk and a group of AI experts and industry executives were the [first ones](https://www.reuters.com/technology/musk-experts-urge-pause-training-ai-systems-that-can-outperform-gpt-4-2023-03-29/) to cite potential risks to society in April.

Recent developments in AI have created tools supporters say can be used in applications from medical diagnostics to writing legal briefs, but this has [sparked fears](https://www.reuters.com/technology/white-house-takes-new-steps-study-ai-risks-determine-impact-workers-2023-05-23/) the technology could lead to privacy violations, power misinformation campaigns, and lead to issues with "smart machines" thinking for themselves.

AI pioneer Hinton earlier [told Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/ai-pioneer-says-its-threat-world-may-be-more-urgent-than-climate-change-2023-05-05/) that AI could pose a "more urgent" threat to humanity than climate change.

Last week OpenAI CEO Sam Altman referred to EU AI - the first efforts to create a regulation for AI - as over-regulation and threatened to leave Europe. He [reversed](https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-has-no-plans-leave-europe-ceo-2023-05-26/) his stance within days after [criticism](https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-ceos-threat-quit-eu-draws-lawmaker-backlash-2023-05-25/) from politicians.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will [meet](https://www.reuters.com/technology/eus-von-der-leyen-meet-openai-ceo-altman-thursday-2023-05-30/) Altman on Thursday.
